originality.rationale: The new statement is simultaneous equality of the two canonical ellipsoids of distinct integral and fractional perfect-matching polytopes, with strict separation of every nontrivial blossom facet from the integral John ball and exact global contact certificates. The primary metric-polytope ellipsoid theorem concerns a different convex body, and established matching-polytope facet/vertex descriptions alone do not imply that exponentially many additional integral facets leave the inner John ellipsoid unchanged. An eigenpolytope polarity computation can partially recover the fractional ellipsoid data, but not strict blossom screening of the integral John ball. Extensive actual semantic, alias and exact-term searching found no covering theorem; earlier equivalent optimal-design work remains an identified risk.
residual_risks: An older or differently named Euclidean inellipsoid/circumellipsoid calculation for the integer one-factor polytope could give the same result; searches cannot establish publication novelty.
The 2023 metric-polytope source motivates the distinct geometric calculation but is not itself a source of perfect-matching facet constraints; earlier literature supplies those inputs.
No external or independent publication-priority or proof audit has been performed.

value.rationale: A natural and exponentially facet-rich integral perfect-matching polytope is strictly smaller than its fractional relaxation yet has identical unique maximal inscribed and minimal enclosing Euclidean ellipsoids for all even N>=6. Precise strict screening of every blossom facet, a fully explicit contact classification, positive moment certificates, and a sharp asymptotic radius ratio explain an intrinsic geometric integrality-invisibility phenomenon. This is a structural theorem rather than a routine parameter substitution or arbitrary low-order computation.
